SC No.7/9.4.2008, three persons, namely Suraj Bhan, Manoj
Kumar and Sunita were found guilty and were convicted under Sections 323, 325 read with Section
34 IPC along with fine and were sentenced as stated above. It would be relevant to refer to the judicial precedents in which the convictions were set aside
based on the compromise:
a). 308-309 of 1980, decided on April 21, 1980, Hon'ble Supreme Court converted the conviction from
307 IPC to 324 IPC and after that based on compromise, accepted the compounding of offence
under section 324 IPC and acquitted the appellants. All the offences for which the appellants are
convicted are compoundable and the compromise can be entered into with the permission of the
court. We accordingly allow the appeal and
set aside the conviction and sentence imposed on both the appellants. Vennila, , the appellants before Hon'ble Supreme Court
had been convicted under Section 494 read with Section 109 of IPC. While observing that the offence involved was compoundable with the wife's consent
and permission of the Court, Hon'ble Supreme Court granted permission to compound the offence,
and resultantly the appellants stood acquitted of the offence for which they have been held guilty. State of Bihar, 2001 AIR (SCW) 5190, out of three convicts, one was
convicted under Section 376 IPC, and the other two were convicted only under Sections 325 & 323
of IPC. Although Hon'ble Supreme Court did not find any scope for granting
special leave by the convict challenging his conviction under section 376 IPC, however, granted the
other permission to the other two convicts to compound the offences under Section 320 (8) of the
Criminal Procedure Code and acquitted both of them. Hon'ble Supreme Court allowed such application for compounding and resultantly acquitted the
g). Indeed in view of the compromise the accused appellants
stand acquitted of the offence under Section 323 Indian Penal Code. 1 and 2 under Section 498A
Indian Penal Code is maintained, but the sentence of imprisonment passed on them for offence
under Section 498-A is reduced to the period already undergone.
